Siddhartha Gadgil said:

Is there a way to cross-reference in a verso document?

Yes! The ref role will do it in the general case. Also, specific kinds of cross-references may have specialized operators - e.g. {tactic}`grind` will cross-reference to the docs for grind in addition to setting up highlighting and hovers.

A thorough treatment of cross-referencing definitely belongs in the user's guide.

As a quick summary: Verso cross-references work more like they do in Sphinx than in LaTeX. Documentation is organized into "domains", which are essentially namespaces, and within a domain, canonical names map to definition sites paired with arbitrary metadata. It's always possible to link to a name from a domain, and it's often possible to find other information as well. All the domains are saved to xref.json in the document root, which allows documents to refer to other documents' items.

David Thrane Christiansen said:

Verso now has a web page, at https://verso.lean-lang.org. I hope it's useful for you.

What additions would you find most valuable?

So, I am finally getting around to the project of trying to properly learn Verso, and one documentation feature that I'm personally finding lacking is a basic tutorial to go from "not having verso tooling installed" to "serving verso-generated pages on a real webpage". This is stuff that I'm sure I can figure out from looking at the example code and experimenting a bit, but I'm a bit disappointed that the "Get Started ->" link on https://verso.lean-lang.org/ goes to a github repo full of templates rather than a friendlier tutorial.

I see that there's a bash script that clones that template repo in response to a basic question about what kind of template the user selects, but I think this is actually too much abstraction for a beginner. I want to understand what the tool is doing in order to gain context, and right now this means I have to look at and understand a bash script, which is kind of annoying. Also, on my system, verso-init.sh actually breaks because of some custom details about how I have git set up on my system - but really I don't think the script should be cloning anything at all, it should be setting up a bare minimum of Lean code to get something rendering and then inviting the user to clone a template themselves.
I might try to submit some PRs once I understand what's going on better.

I agree that a web page would be nicer than a README for this.

Is there something that I can update in the script to make it also work on your machine?

In any case, I think it's totally reasonable not to want to run a script like this. I went ahead and set it up so each release tag also creates a GitHub release with a downloadable tarball/zip file for each template that's set up the way that the script would set it up.

Here's the most recent release.

I didn't get that badly stuck - the specific problem I ran into was that on this line: https://github.com/leanprover/verso-templates/blob/main/verso-init.sh#L236 the bash script calls git commit, and on my system I have my .gitconfig set up to require explicitly setting a git identity on a per-repo basis (because I use several git identities on a regular basis and I want to make sure I know which one I use with which repo). So the script failed on my system and I had to spend some time figuring out what had happened and manually fixing it, which was annoying but also specific to my configuration.

But I think the broader problem is that the way for beginners to get bootstrapped into verso shouldn't be by running a bash script that sets up an environment for them; it should be a simple tutorial document (which could be in the README file) that explains how to install the verso tooling on their system and then use it to build a simple site without the use of a pre-made template at all. The point is to tell the beginner what commands to run but have them actually run the commands themselves, so they can start building intuition about how verso works; instead of having to debug what the bash script or template is doing.
